title: The Cybernetic Unconscious: Lacanian Psychoanalysis as Architecture for Artificial Intelligence Systems
content: This essay proposes that the correspondence between Lacan's three registers, the Real, the Symbolic and the Imaginary, and the layers of an artificial intelligence system for psychoanalytic research can be read as a structural analogy, under defined constraints, rather than a loose metaphor. Building on this analogy, I construct a four-layer data architecture organised according to the RSI registers together with a Layer of the Other, and four processing agents organised according to Lacan's Four Discourses, whose succession I name the Gira Discursiva, a functional cycle inspired by these four discourses and by the quart de tour of Seminar XVII, without claiming to reproduce its exact algebraic sequence. I propose three concepts: the cybernetic unconscious, the Gira Discursiva, and prompt engineering as enunciation. I argue that the unconscious, as Lacan formalised it (a signifying chain subject to combinatory laws), offers software engineering a more fecund organising heuristic than the single-label modelling I first adopted, for domains where knowing is not transparent. I argue that computational formalisation need not betray Lacanian theory; pursued with care, it can force a conceptual precision that illuminates aspects of the theory which purely textual exegesis may leave in shadow.
